description: The Harte Research Institute publishes modelled socioeconomic consequences of northern Gulf of Mexico storm-surge flooding. GRIIDC identifies 241 component files representing twenty-nine shapefiles, covering buildings, vehicles, roads, bridges, essential facilities, wastewater assets, displaced people and shelter needs. HAZUS-MH 4.2.3 calculations combine 1% and 0.2% annual-exceedance floodplains with 0.2, 0.5, 1.2 and 2.0 m sea-level-rise scenarios for 2100. The repository resource is publicly and freely available, with CC0 stated in the describing article. Its regional outputs can benchmark loss and emergency-response simulations. Results depend on floodplain and exposure assumptions and do not predict realised damage. The related platform-hazus describes the loss-estimation software used to generate these scenarios.
